correctness.rationale: The count process is a finite killed continuous-time Markov chain. Each walker jumps at total rate 1, with killing rate c_1/2. Each independent reset clock contributes a separate single-coordinate jump. Invertible A=-Q_0 yields exact u=A^{-1}1 and v=A^{-1}Bu; analyticity in r gives v(start)=M_N'(0+). Exact rational arithmetic checks Au=1 and Av=Bu at every count state for N=1..5, reproduces all fractions/signs, and independently builds the full labeled Markov chain for N=1..3. No extrapolation beyond five walkers or global-optimum claim.

value.rationale: Independent reset clocks are a natural design mechanism in parallel search. On the canonical five-vertex path, the first loss of local reset benefit occurs at the exact finite cutoff of five searchers, whereas common-clock resetting has a different cutoff on the same path. The distinction is not cosmetic: the count generator has separate reset transitions, and the N=4 sign changes across mechanisms. This is a meaningful finite benchmark of mechanism-dependent first-detection sensitivity, without needing a broad asymptotic theorem.
